notes.title: Wayward Strand - One Year Anniversary!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

It’s incredible to think that it’s already been a year since we put Wayward Strand out into the world. We’ve been so chuffed with the response that you all have had to this experience we created together, and thought it’d be lovely to reminisce about what’s happened during Wayward Strand’s first year, as well as giving an update on where we, the people who made it, are at!

First things first, to celebrate Wayward Strand’s release anniversary, we’re doing a pretty big sale - our [b]first 40% discount[/b]. If Wayward Strand sounds interesting to you, or you've had your eye on it for a while, but weren't entirely sure about it, now is a great time to get your copy and give it a try!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1080450/Wayward_Strand/

[h2]One year ago...[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/bf91bd6cc0be780db670b769a4868ea8eb8c5196.jpg[/img]
[i]The team on launch day! September 15, 2022
[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/1e118fc548275dd270872ba902b0d9bb39921da1.jpg[/img]
[i]Our launch party a couple of weeks later.
[/i]


After seven long years, we finally released Wayward Strand out into the world on September 15, 2022. We were so proud of getting it out there, and made sure to celebrate!

Right out of the gate were the AGDAs (Australian Game Development Awards), where we were nominated for storytelling and serious games, and the Golden Joystick Awards, with a nomination for best storytelling. We presented Wayward Strand at PAX Australia the next month, both with a booth at PAX Together, and a really wonderful panel where we discussed the game’s development.

It’s been so wonderful every time that we’ve gotten to show the game since it’s released, to have players come up to us and talk with us about their experiences with the game, and how it made them feel - PAX Together was the first moment where that happened, and it was incredibly lovely to hear from all of you, and to talk with you.

[h2]The press...[/h2]

As the game was launching, we also started to see the reviews coming in. We didn’t really know what reviewers would think of the game - they play and write about so many games every year, so we had no idea whether they’d have time for our (honestly a bit strange) experience, where we ask quite a lot of the player - in a pretty much objective-less experience, it’s up to you to explore the game and discover things for yourself.

But we were really pleasantly surprised how many reviewers and journalists got what we were trying to do. We were covered a ton in international media, often with people talking about how Wayward Strand made them [url=https://www.vooks.net/wayward-strand-review/]feel things[/url] that no other game had made them feel; how it’s a [url=https://uppercutcrit.com/review-wayward-strand-is-a-new-classic-of-video-game-storytelling/]step in a new direction[/url] for story-focused games; or how it made them want to [url=https://kotaku.com/wayward-strand-impressions-australia-adventure-1849533769]call their grandma[/url].

We really appreciate how so many reviewers played and enjoyed the game on its own merit, instead of focusing on comparing it with other games, which doesn’t really make much sense to do with Wayward Strand, because it (and we) are trying to create such a different experience to so many other games.

The positivity was such that we ended up in several ‘best games of the year’ list, including the top Switch games on Metacritic for 2022, and the [url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/story/2022-12-14/the-most-memorable-narratives-of-2022-were-the-ones-that-were-playable]LA Times’ most memorable narratives of 2022[/url].

[h2]2023[/h2]

[previewyoutube=Cqr-p0-7yjo;full][/previewyoutube]

2023 has been a wonderful year so far - the biggest thing is that we’ve gotten to talk about Wayward Strand a lot more, now that it’s out and people can play it! After being [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oGlLYmW-zTo]interviewed by Alanah Pearce[/url] and appearing on the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=80BmCfiK860]Eggplant Show[/url], Georgia and Jason did a talk at GDC that focused on the narrative and NPC development of Wayward Strand, which is now on [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cqr-p0-7yjo]Youtube[/url]. (A clip from that talk recently got a lot of attention on [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@official_gdc/video/7270150982758042922]TikTok[/url]!)

[previewyoutube=80BmCfiK860;full][/previewyoutube]

We were also nominated for the A MAZE awards, and Goldie and Jason got the chance to do [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=80BmCfiK860]a talk[/url] about why we love frustrating the player. (Thank you again to the audience for some lovely and thought-provoking questions!)

[h2]A few last things to note![/h2]

While we’re still progressing on an update to the game that would introduce within-day saving, due to Life Stuff (including some extended trips and one of the team’s family getting a new member), work on that version will be pausing for the next couple of months, and then after that there’s still quite a bit more work to go before it's done. So, we’re still hopeful that it’ll make it out there eventually, but wanted to bo honest in saying that we can’t make any promises on how soon.

Also, we’ve had quite a few people ask us about our next plans - we can't say too much just yet, except that we've got Some Stuff in the works, and that the team love each other and are excited to get to work together again! It's been an interesting year, as we've scattered a bit to work on different other projects and at different companies, but what we've been finding is that we're still committed and excited to get together again on more projects.

Thanks so much for your interest in Wayward Strand, and your support of one-of-a-kind experiences like this, made by independent game artists that are exploring new territories in interactive storytelling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/1ea085574cf18be4fc53153da89d30b791c364f5.png[/img]

notes.title: Spring Sale Discount, GDC Talks, Nominations and more!
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow Wayward Strand enthusiasts! We're here to share some exciting news and updates with you about the game and our studio, [i]ghost pattern[/i]. We've had a lot going on lately, from GDC talks to award nominations, and we're thrilled to share all the details with you.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1080450/Wayward_Strand/

The first big news is that Wayward Strand is [b]currently on sale[/b] as part of the Steam Spring Sale, at a discount of 20%. This is a great opportunity to pick up the game at a reduced price and experience the beautiful, interactive storytelling that we've poured our hearts into.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/c9e4b8d9668cd80078a13f30e1934b566d96545c.jpg[/img]

Also, if you played Wayward Strand and loved it (thank you!!), [b]leaving us a review, even a short one[/b], is a [b]massive help[/b] for us with our first, self-published game! We'd love to create more innovative and truly original experiences like Wayward Strand, and having lots of positive reviews would be a huge help in getting us there.

[h1]Talks at GDC![/h1]

Another bit of news is that we're headed to the [url=https://gdconf.com/]Game Developers Conference[/url] (GDC) in San Francisco next week. Jason and Georgia will be delivering a talk titled "The Secret Lives of NPCs", where they'll dive into the structure and production of the unique narrative mechanics in Wayward Strand. 

If you're interested in narrative focused game development, digital storytelling, or just want to know more about our game, and you're heading to GDC, we'd love for you to join us there. You can find more information about the talk and how to attend on the [url=https://schedule.gdconf.com/session/independent-games-summit-the-secret-lives-of-npcs-wayward-strand/892898]GDC schedule page[/url].

Additionally, Maize and Tfer, leads on our audio team, will be delivering a talk called "[url=https://schedule.gdconf.com/session/audio-summit-an-important-conversation-about-conversations/892067]An Important Conversation about Conversations[/url]," which focuses on the production pipelines and experiences of recording almost 20,000 lines of dialogue for Wayward Strand. Doing this recording with on a shoestring budget and ending up with such incredible quality VO is a monumental feat for a small indie studio like ours, and we're excited to share our process and insights with the community.

Both talks are happening on Tuesday at 10:50 AM, so mark your calendars and join us if you can. And, if we’re able to share the recordings in the future we will be sure to do so.

[h1]More Awards![/h1]

In other (and also good) news, we're pleased and humbled to announce that Wayward Strand has been [b]nominated for an AMAZE award![/b] The AMAZE award recognises innovative and groundbreaking games from all over the world, and we're honoured to be included alongside the other incredible titles. 

We'd like to give a special shoutout to WINGS fund, who support the category we were nominated in. The fund focuses on supporting and empowering women-led studios, and it's an incredible and generous resource for our industry. See the full list of incredible nominees [url=https://2023.amaze-berlin.de/nominees/]here[/url].

[h1]Cool other stuff from the Wayward Team[/h1]

But that's not all! We'd love to share the brand new trailer for our collaborator Olivia Haines' new video game, Surf Club.

[previewyoutube=Byo8f6v8TxY;full][/previewyoutube]

Olivia is an incredibly talented game developer and artist, and we're honoured to have worked with her on Wayward Strand. Surf Club looks absolutely stunning, and we can't wait to play it ourselves. You can wishlist it on Steam now!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1685740/Surf_Club/
 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/c271c72d876037a36a8e1605405faee9e1e6ce21.png[/img]

 
And a final note that Wayward Strand post-launch development is still ongoing, and we're working hard to add more save-load functionality to the game. We'll have more information to share soon, so stay tuned.

We hope you're all as excited as we are about these updates and news. Thank you so much for your ongoing support of [i]ghost pattern[/i] and Wayward Strand - we couldn't do it without you!

notes.title: Spring Down Under for the Steam Fall Festival
notes.content:
[h3]Hello![/h3]

It's Goldie!
I hope you’re cosy and wrapped up in various blankets, hoodies, oodies, onesies or jumpers right now, because it’s time for the [b]Steam Autumn Festival![/b]
My [i]very[/i] witty title would have worked better if they’d called it the Steam Fall Festival, but I appreciate the language too. Autumn just has a nice ring to it, don’t you think? 

[i]Autumn. [/i]

Makes me think of all of the best parts. From the chilly, crisp air, to the warm ciders, grey skies…Beautiful golden leaves, darkening evenings. Late season honey, pumpkin soup, apple pie…and of course, videogames on sale [i]uwu[/i].

We’re dipping our toes into the world of sales - we’re offering a [b]10% discount[/b] on Wayward Strand this week - not bad! [i]Maybe it’s time to pick it up, or maybe now is a good time to tell a friend or family member about us?[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/c997ccd4025c5dabaab35eddbd01d0b2ec043af6.png[/img]

Ok I’ll fess up, it’s actually spring in Melbourne! We’re climbing out of winter (allegedly), but boy is it still cold, wet, windy. [i]Almost as if…the climate has…changed?[/i] Nevertheless, it’s been lovely having lighter evenings.  And some of the days have been glorious - warm sunshine, flowers popping off.

So how are we going? Pretty good. [i]Busy![/i]

[h2]What have we been working on?[/h2]

[h3]Saves[/h3]

The big one is saves. We definitely heard you loud and clear that we need more save points!

I want to be upfront: I, Goldie, am not a programmer. I usually do the art stuff for the game, so I won’t be the best person to speak to the[i] technical particulars[/i] but I do understand that there’s a good reason that implementing saves into Wayward Strand has been quite tricky. I think it’s likely to do with needing to work out a way to let the game know WHERE every single character is at any point in time, as well as WHAT information that character has about you - what did you say to them, what have they said to you, do you know X, and have they told you their thoughts on it or not? What did you say to someone else and how does that impact them?
All of that sort of stuff.
Honestly, I’m sure it’s complicated.

If you’re curious about this work, I definitely invite you to [url=https://discord.gg/Qe6C6R4yP7]come to our discord[/url] and chat about it with the people who are working at it.

We’ve also been busy with patches of course! There are a few blog posts here on Steam outlining changes we’ve already pushed, if you’d like to check those out. Off the top of my head, there have been standard bug fixes, and we’ve also unlocked a few achievements which weren’t possible to get (they are now all possible to get!) And of course there's been the big change of letting players load in to any of the three days once they’ve completed a full playthrough.
You can always see our [url=https://waywardstrand.com/patchinfo/]full patch notes here.[/url]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]
Speaking of achievements, a bloody huge congratulations to UnbrokenOdds who, as far as we know, was the first person to ‘100%’ Wayward Strand, in a way. They’ve collected all of our achievements which is a ridiculously big achievement in itself. I can’t imagine how many hours they played to do that! Well done to UnbrokenOdds, and to everyone else who is getting close, or who may have done it by the time I’ve posted this blog. Inspirational!


[h2]What else?[/h2]

[list]
[*] Well, as usual I’m going to remind you that reviews really help - we don’t have many but we’re reading them all and being filled with warm feelings, and appreciate each one. If you have 5 minutes and could sling a review on Steam, that would be super great!
[*] Our other request is to think about anyone in your life who you think might be a good fit for Wayward Strand. If you’ve played it, you know that it’s highly accessible, and perhaps especially to people new to games. Maybe you have a family member who would like it?
[*] We’ve been enjoying watching everyone Stream the game - get in touch if you’re on Twitch! The best place to get in touch is probably over on Twitter @WaywardStrand.
[/list]

[h1]Oh![/h1]

[h3]We've been nominated for a Golden Joystick![/h3]
Did I write about that in another blog? Freakin’ wild. What a huge honour to be nominated for Best Storytelling - like…the games we are alongside are so, so great. It really made us feel proud and excited. At the time of posting, the ceremony is just 2 hours away - you can watch the award show at 12PM PST November 22 on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/goldenjoystickawards]Twitch[/url] or [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qcYAU1c0lMk]YouTube[/url].


[h3]Jumplight Odyssey[/h3]

Finally, did you know that our very own Jason was lead developer for League of Geek's amazing debut game Armello? Well, he was! League of Geeks have just announced a VERY cool looking game (two games, actually, but I'm gonna talk about the one with a badass space captain princess).

[i]"Keep hope alive on your adventure to the mythical Forever Star! Gather survivors, repair and build out your starship, brave black holes, and fend off attacks, all while managing the daily soap opera of your colorful crew."[/i]

Kinda seems like Rimworld meets Two Point Hospital? Neato!

Check it out here: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1893820/Jumplight_Odyssey/
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]



Anyhew, I will wrap this up, much like the gifts I'll be wrapping this time next month! [i]Exciting times![/i]

Love you, thanks for being here.

Goldie & [i]ghost pattern.[/i]

PS: [i]Steam backend can be quite confusing, so if this blog post disappears after the sale ends, I'll repost the newsy bits as a general update <3
[/i]

[b]TL;DR[/b]
Steam Autumn Sale.
Wayward Strand 10% off!
Starts: Tuesday, November 22 at 10 AM PST (Nov 23rd 5 AM GMT+11)
Ends: Tuesday, November 29 at 10 AM PST (Nov 30th 5 AM GMT+11)

notes.title: Patch v1.0.4 live on Steam!
notes.content:
Hi all!

We've been chipping away at a bunch more fixes that players have been finding post-launch, and have bundled them into [b]Patch 1.0.4[/b]; this includes a few issues that have been found by some diligent achievement hunters on our Discord - thanks to community members [b]unbrokenodds[/b] and [b]andre.[/b] in particular for the help! Speaking of the Discord, if you wanted to chat with us and other players about the game (or about your favourite '70s kitsch), you can [b]join our Discord[/b] with this link: https://discord.gg/KDAMU3N 

What we discovered when fixing the achievements is that some weren't accessible due to whole scenes not occurring; with over 1000 scenes in the game, we knew that there'd be some that wouldn't play for whatever reason, but it's exciting to say that there are now [b]several additional scenes and sections of scenes that can be found[/b].

We don't want to spoil too much, particularly because some relate to storylines that are hidden away in the game, but let's just say that fans of a particular character should make sure to hang out with them in their room on Day 3...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/4e0203edf96d15c6bb04823d2d25a04420db1384.png[/img]

[h2]Roadmap
[/h2]

As per the roadmap in the previous update, improved saving is still slated for a future patch; the team are working on Wayward Strand alongside other work at the moment, so we aren't able to get updates out quickly, but we'll keep chipping away at them!

[h2]Patch v1.0.4 Notes
[/h2]

Here's the full list of fixes and improvements that we've done in this patch:

[list]
[*] The Iilk storyline can now be experienced in full, and the 'Iilk Fan' achievement/trophy can now be correctly attained.
[*] When the appropriate conditions are met, Casey is actually given the option to "tell a white lie", and the 'White Lie' achievement/trophy can now be correctly attained.
[*] More opportunity is now given for Casey to follow up on Margot's request, to ensure that it's reasonably possible for the 'Careful With Your Words' achievement/trophy to be attained.
[*] Fixes an issue where, after 5:30pm, the potential things that Casey or other characters could say and do were being significantly curtailed.
[*] Casey should no longer become stuck when accompanying Lily during her afternoon rounds on the first day.
[*] During Lily's afternoon rounds on the first day, improvements have been made to the scene direction, and how Casey is managed, in Tomi's room.
[*] On day 2, when Joe is helping Esther from the cafeteria, he will no longer float and the wheelchair will not appear in duplicate.
[*] On day 2, when Casey is changing the record for Mr Pruess, she will now walk around Mr Pruess, instead of through him, and her bag won't float.
[*] During day 2, Casey should no longer get stuck with Ted for long periods.
[*] At the end of day 2, Casey should no longer become stuck by the nurse's station if she's around when Ruth calls in.
[*] Casey won't running ahead of Tomi, when choosing to follow her.
[*] Ted will no longer try to start a conversation with Casey, when she's on the far side of the cafeteria.
[*] Increases audibility of Neil, when Lily is attempting to cheer him up on day 3.
[*] Increases audibility of dialogue between Casey and Ida when Casey is departing Ida's room.
[*] Casey should no longer be given the option to pick up a book, if she is already holding soup.
[*] Fixes props being in an inconsistent state on day 3, if transformed by story events on day 2.
[*] Resolves some more instances of characters talking over themselves.
[*] Minor improvements to story logic.
[*] Minor improvements to scene timing and direction.
[*] Fixes typos.
[*] Players will no longer have the option to start from a chapter if the required save data is missing.
[*] Players will no longer get stuck in loading, when attempting to load a save file that doesn't exist.
[*] Hitting the back button will now correctly leave the chapter select screen.
[/list]

That's all for now! Oh, we also wanted to thank everyone for the lovely reviews that they've been leaving for the game on our Store Page - we've been highlighting some of our favourites on our Twitter:   https://twitter.com/WaywardStrand

If you've played Wayward Strand and liked it, it would be hugely helpful if you could spend a few moments to [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1080450/Wayward_Strand/]leave us a review[/url][/b]; we're a small indie team, and really appreciate your support <3

notes.title: Patch v1.0.3 now available on Steam
notes.content:
Hey everyone - first, thanks so much for all the kind words about Wayward Strand so far! It's wonderful to hear you all connecting with it and discovering so much within the game.

We have prepared our first post-launch patch, and it's now live on Steam! This is mainly just a few key fixes for issues that players have found in the live version, along with a small quality-of-life feature.

Oh, a quick note that while the patch is called 1.0.3, it's the first post-launch patch - we did a couple of additional patches pre-launch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/1976609e32175c3876fc8260ef6995f70148ac7b.jpg[/img]

[h2]Chapter Select[/h2]
We've added a feature which allows you to choose which Chapter to load into - this will load the game up into the most recent save file for that chapter. This allows you to eg. start your most recent playthrough again from Day 2, or to play Day 3 several times over. 

This will be handy for folks that are trying to unlock particular achievements, or who are mapping out what happens on each day in the game - or just for if you're keen to try one of the later Days again without having to play Day 1 all over again.

[h2]Roadmap[/h2]
We've also begun work on the most requested feature so far, which is midday saves. We don't have an ETA for when this will make it into a patch, as it's a significant amount of work to implement and test, but wanted to mention that work has begun on this feature, and we'll be continuing that work as we can.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/8d22fda60c6c1c0a6ac5fb1d76331f4e75a7a3fc.gif[/img]

[h2]Patch v1.0.3 Notes
[/h2]	[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Mrs Beaumaris’s levitating clipboard at the end of Day 1 should no longer exist.
[*] Casey now puts the shield in her satchel when the player selects that option.
[*] Fixed an issue where both Joe and Casey could think that they had taken Mr Pruess back to his room on Day 1.
[*] Mr Pettigrew now remembers that he’s met you if he sees you at the nurse’s station on Day 2 afternoon.
[*] Fixed an issue where Dr Bouchard and Lily would say each other’s lines for a bit on Day 1 afternoon, and ensured Casey’s satchel wouldn’t do a little dance if she was in the room with Dr Bouchard during this scene.
[*] Casey can no longer steal a teacup from Ida’s room when Ida suggests that you go see Mr Avery.
[*] Ida’s knitting should no longer disconnect from her knitting needles and float up into the air.
[*] Joe should no longer snap into the floor when giving Esther their meds on Day 2.
[*] On Day 2, if you’re standing at the nurse’s station in the late afternoon, you should no longer be stuck there in some situations.
[*] Fixed an issue where on the afternoon of Day 1, Lily would talk with Casey about Ms Hummel as if they hadn’t met, even if they’d all had lunch together.
[*] Fixed several spots where characters wouldn’t have their prop states correctly restored at the end of a scene - characters in the Cafeteria should hang on to their spoons more consistently now.
[*] Ms Hummel should no longer sit inside the table, or off in the middle of nowhere, in the Cafeteria.
[*] Fixed the overlapping dialogue in Mr Pettigrew and Mrs Beaumaris’s phone conversation on Day 1, and in the Day 2 evening scene with Mrs Beaumaris.
[*] Fixed some spots where Casey would write things down in her Notebook without having seen them.
[*] On Day 3 afternoon, Ms Hummel will no longer teleport her watering can to herself, and waters her plants instead of watering Casey.
[*] Ensured that the options display correctly when Lily offers Casey the glass of orange juice in Esther’s room on Day 1.
[*] Ensuring that Casey actually refills Ms Hummel’s watering can on Day 2, if Tomi isn’t in the room and the player selects that option.
[*] On Day 3 evening, Casey now puts the scarf into her bag, instead of her shirt pocket.
[*] Fixed some spelling mistakes.
[*] Improved audio levels for the records that are played in the Lounge.
[/list]
	[h3]Game Menus[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a chapter select screen, allowing the player to replay from the start of each chapter, once they've already played that chapter once and have a save file for it.
[*] Updated credits
[/list]

notes.title: Wayward Strand: Best Narrative at the Australian Game Design Awards nomination!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

[b]IT IS LAUNCH WEEK[/b]

First up, check out this short and sweet video which shows some [i]emotional content[/i] from the team

[previewyoutube=IYOclzxG-rk;full][/previewyoutube]


Second up,

It's AGDAs time, baby!

We are incredibly honoured to have been nominated in a few categories - as well as given an honourable mention for another.

We are nominated for [b]Best Narrative[/b], along with friends [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1776160/You_Will_Not_Remain/]You Will (Not) Remain[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1896700/Wylde_Flowers/]Wylde Flowers[/url]

We are also nominated for [b]Best Serious Game[/b], along with friends again (how lucky are we?) [url=https://www.playkinderworld.com/]Kinder World[/url] and [url=https://raw-emotions.phoria.com.au/]RAW: Emotions Unite Us[/url]

Finally, we have been awarded an honourable mention in the [b]Accessibility [/b]category, thanks so much to our fantastic accessibility consultant, [url=https://twitter.com/catrelatedpun]Cameron Hopkinson[/url] for their work on Wayward Strand there.

After many years of developing, plus a few stuck inside, we are [i]very[/i] ready to let our hair down and have a boogie at the AGDAs this October.

notes.title: Cast Announcement for Wayward Strand
notes.content:
G'day!

As per usual, let's get right down to the meat and potatoes of this post: our cast!
[h2]
[b]Here's the announcement in video form[/b][/h2]

[previewyoutube=CRakxiogsA0;full][/previewyoutube]


We want to start off with a huge shout-out to our four studios - Original Score in Melbourne, ZigZag Post in Sydney, Innenhof in Vienna and Voiceover Soho in London. Making people on three continents sound like they’re in one room is *hard*, but our audio director Maize Wallin and their team have had some of the best quality sound to work with, thanks to the hard work of everyone around the world who collaborated with us!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]

[h2]Without further ado...[/h2]
[i]It’s finally, FINALLY time to announce our fantastic cast! We don’t wanna wait one second longer, let’s just do it.
[/i]

First cab off the rank: this one's no secret. Reprising her role from our 2019 demo, we have the inimitable [b]Anne Charleston[/b] in the role of [b]Ida Vaughan[/b]! Although many of you have recognised her from her iconic role as Madge on Neighbours, Anne has had a stellar international career in theatre, film and TV across Australia, the UK and Ireland. Working with such a legend of the industry was such a joy!

We're so excited to introduce our [b]Esther Fitzgerald - Michela Ledwidge![/b] She's a director in her own right, working across all visual and digital media. Michela put so much consideration and research into her portrayal of our beloved Esther, and it shows - playtesters are already falling in love with this character!

We were honoured to work with [b]Shane Clayton[/b], playing the role of [b]Ted Muir.[/b] Shane is a young Bunurong man, a performer, and an absolute delight! He brought spades of humour to the recording studio, and so much warmth and heart to the character of Ted.

Ahhhh, Mr Pruess. He's the character who has *easily* changed the most as a result of voiceover. When we wrote this character, we thought he was cold, inscrutable, solitary. But [b]Erhard Hartmann [/b]infused[b] Heinrich Pruess [/b]with such incredible joy, and truly brought the character to life - all the way from Austria! Erhard is a prominent actor in Austria and Germany, and we were so lucky to work with him - not least because he let us know that we had accidentally named one of our characters quite a rude word in German, which we were then able to fix!

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/e385a9b440a2099785183b66862ca34d98fdbafa.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/a873f13d60b505a36bbf46991bab8c4b7a469e9f.png[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/1ea085574cf18be4fc53153da89d30b791c364f5.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/fda3bc581cacede721fed738f0069cd4f22a8960.png[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/4c40c86d61ab5d4b8d055278da6bc0a0bae970e4.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/71e813e0afc968910b77b8ea7c11ef2d583eee41.png[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/9a25b651f196f9937e489096bdf9d5fd3111a31a.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/428b9cc7f686889f60dcae3d210efc0832242c5b.png[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/4e0203edf96d15c6bb04823d2d25a04420db1384.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/ee6bb7561bd6f3cfc520afba88bcab803c5d301b.png[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/d8aebe0602286d892ef0aab290446ebec570415c.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/231abb6ddbabe668a4746053660680b737205989.png[/img][/url][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/0b05112344f760831195e112a1de268fd4a1ac0c.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/e7aad1645021b22554cf945f77a5f29b98bd6a19.png[/img][/url]

It's been hard to keep this one to ourselves… the loquacious [b]Neil Avery[/b] will be voiced by none other than living legend [b]Michael Caton[/b]! You'll remember him from The Castle, or The Sullivans, or Last Cab to Darwin, but in truth, if you live in Australia and you own a TV, you can guarantee his face has been on it. Michael was so down-to-earth in the studio - quite the opposite of his character!

Next, another performer returning from our 2019 demo. [b]Ruth Beaumaris[/b] will be played by [b]Jenny Seedsman[/b]! Neighbours, Blue Heelers, State Coroner - you name it, she's been in it. Jenny brought a lot of care and warmth to the character of Ruth, even in her sternest moments!

The director of the hospital,[b] Felix Pettigrew[/b], is warm, energetic, and always immaculately dressed. Bringing his infectious effervescence to this role is [b]Josiah Lulham![/b] Josiah wears many hats, as a theatre actor, a facilitator, and an anthropology scholar. We could barely get a clean take with Josiah, with how much he was making us laugh in the studio!

Our Celtic Cuisinier may be shrouded in mystery in the game, but we can finally reveal his identity in real life.[b] John Barrett[/b] is the voice of [b]Devin the cook![/b] John also helped us add some Irish language to the game, which was a real treat.

Sticking with hospital staff, nurse [b]Lily Marshall[/b] will be played by [b]Harriet Wallace-Mead! [/b]Harriet is an actor, a producer, and also a horticulturalist! Harriet is another actor that we worked with on our 2019 demo, and when we were casting for the final game, she was one of the first performers we decided on - Lily just wouldn't be Lily without this voice!

In Wayward Strand, Lily works closely with another nurse, [b]Joe Tagliabue[/b], played by the wonderful [b]Peter Paltos[/b]. Apart from being an experienced and gifted actor, Peter also happens to be a healthcare worker! So he was able to bring so much wisdom and insight to this performance.

For some reason, we decided to record one of our saddest storylines on our very first day of recording. Thankfully, we were recording the delightful [b]Jennifer Vuletic[/b] for the role of [b]Dr Margot Bouchard[/b], who brought so much power and humanity to one of our more heartbreaking characters (you'll see). From our first meeting with Jennifer, she was so positive about our work, which meant so much to us as a team. And I think we all shed a tear or two in the studio!

Dr Shen, our last staff member to reveal! [b]Celine Shen[/b] is played by [b]Renee Lim[/b], who, believe it or not, is both a practising actor [i]AND[/i] a practising doctor! So this role was a walk in the park for Renee, and she was another performer who was able to bring such a depth of subject matter knowledge to bear on her role.
[h2]
Last, but certainly not least, [/h2]the player character; fourteen-year-old [b]Casey Beaumaris[/b]. It is such an incredible honour to introduce you to [b]Nancy Curtis.[/b] Intelligence. Humour. Work ethic. Nancy recorded a whopping 1200+ pages of dialogue in just 10 studio sessions. And she did it all with such ease. When we first heard a recording of Nancy, we thought Casey herself had escaped from the game and come to life. Working with Nancy was a true delight, and one of the highlights of making this game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/87ab08b703f781c2333ae23e21db0a4b92697455.png[/img]

13 actors announced so far… are there any others? I guess you'll have to just wait and play the game to find out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]

I can't believe we're just 4 weeks out from launch.
Absolutely so excited my socks are falling off.

See you there!
Lots of love,
Goldie.

notes.title: Wayward Strand - Launch Delay Announcement
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

[h3]There’s been some news, which is a bit of a relief for us. I’ll cut to the chase: we’re delaying the release of Wayward Strand.[/h3]

[h1] [b]We will now release on September 15![/b][/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/0b05112344f760831195e112a1de268fd4a1ac0c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]

It was a difficult decision to make, because this project has gone on a long time already - some of you will have been waiting for it since we were in the showcase at PAX Melbourne in 2019, some will have been waiting since we showed it at Freeplay Parallels in 201...7? Really?

And on our end, we've been so keen for it to be out in the world!

[b]So, why the delay?[/b]

In truth, very few games like Wayward Strand exist. When you set the timelines for making a new game, you might think about other similar games you’ve heard about or worked on. You might try to compare in your mind how long similar things have taken in the past. So, when we set out to make Wayward Strand, we had a think about similar games...

Games with [b]25,000+ lines of voiceover dialogue[/b]…
… and with all action taking place within [b]real-time mechanics[/b]…
… and with [b]14 characters[/b], each with their [b]own[/b] 3-hour-long in-game journey…
… and with [i]richly [/i]decorated and [i]intensely[/i] researched 3-storey doll-house worlds…
… and with a focus on [b]heartfelt stories[/b], where the nod of a head or a momentary pause between dialogue can make a [i]world[/i] of meaning…
… and all made by a small, self-published indie team ːsteamthumbsupː

As you can imagine, we were left scratching our heads. Regardless, we did our best to set realistic timelines. But as we review each scene in the game and how it all comes together, we felt it was important to spend some additional time to bring the experience closer to our vision. We're doing our best to bring our characters and stories to life for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]

This delay means we can release Wayward Strand at a level of quality that we're very happy with. Importantly, it also allows us to do it in a [i]less stressful[/i] way for the team. Wayward Strand is a game about care, and it would make no sense to make this game without caring for each other. From day one, we’ve been rigorously committed to empathy, openness, and anti-crunch. Game releases are almost always stressful and difficult for the teams behind them, so we're trying to find ways of approaching our release that reduce some of those pressures.

We’ve had so much excitement and support from people like you who are looking forward to playing our game. This support is something we cherish so dearly. Thank you for being caring and patient with us. We are so looking forward to sharing the game with you.


Thanks, love,
ghost pattern

[b] PS. [/b]Coming up later in the month, we'll be announcing our fabulous cast! Keep your eye out <3

notes.title: Wayward Strand announces a July 21st, 2022 release date!
notes.content:
[h1]You’re here! [/h1] 

[h3]Welcome![/h3] It’s thrilling for our little team to see so many of you coming to visit our Steam page. 
We’ve just announced our launch date, and we can’t wait to finally be able to share the game with you.

I’m Georgia, one of the lead writers for Wayward Strand.

[h2]First things first: [/h2]

The game will launch here on Steam, on [b]Thursday 21st July, 2022! [/b]

[hr][/hr] 
For any newcomers, Wayward Strand is a heartfelt narrative game developed in Melbourne, Australia. It’s set here in Australia, in the 70s. You play as Casey, a curious and compassionate 14-year-old who’s spending a few days helping her Mum at the local hospital - which just happens to be on a floating airship above a small regional town.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/dd26b54e604362fc15cbba2c574a1067a1be4a53.gif[/img]

For me, this game is all about care. Casey’s task is deceptively simple - sit with the patients in the elderly ward, and take care of them. Like other adventure games, there is the occasional mystery to uncover or puzzle to solve. But the beating heart of the game is an experience of[b] listening, [/b]of [b]gentleness,[/b] and of the distinct rewards of discovering that everyone around you has their own [b]rich interior world.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/0634a671b11da3ed01793773c8cdc36dadcb4741.gif[/img]

Our team at Ghost Pattern is tiny. Starting with a core team of 5 back in 2016, we’ve roped in a handful of local collaborators to bring this enormous game to life. [b]Featuring 15 characters, over 20,000 lines of voiceover dialogue and a richly illustrated four-storey hospital environment to explore,[/b] the final product looks like the work of a much bigger team! But we’ve all poured our guts into this game, because we know it’ll be unlike [i]anything[/i] you’ve ever played before. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/dfcc0fa5d2b7ac250c66c1930ef585f70e746de2.gif[/img]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Please enjoy these latest screenshots![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/a72473dae16913d5339d2710a0a2606c4bb74ba5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/e8f7272b811f26d38b3cc13a6c86fdced4ec8ab1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/a4ee722e7998f71c6982fb69dd1ac4ffa50d9091.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/193482fc043917a547a5251589405cc96a901da8.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/fb67b65fbfde6e413f1af8af305ba22d157aeea7.png[/img]

[hr][/hr]
Something exciting about this game is that we have carefully designed it with first-time players in mind. Got someone in your life who thinks they’re “not a gamer” or couldn’t enjoy video games? Our game is the perfect place to dip your toe into the world of narrative games. 

With a [b]simple and intuitive UI,[/b] you could sit with a younger sibling, a parent or a grandparent, and explore the gentle world of Wayward Strand together. You could even play together over a cup of tea!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/e12302a2bbc6f24ca55297bfa08e45ab3c95200b.gif[/img]

Finally, Here's a short video we prepared which shows off some of the[b] new VO[/b] in the game.
https://youtu.be/0Q1Wu0o1Avg 
[hr][/hr]
So go ahead and wishlist the game, if you haven’t done already, and have a think about who in your life you’d like to share the experience with.

[h2]We can’t wait to share it with you 
on [b]Thursday 21st July![/b][/h2]

Thanks for your support, everyone.
Georgia

notes.title: Melbourne International Games Week - NEW DEMO!
notes.content:
First of all:

[h3][i] [b]We have a new demo, available to play right now![/b][/i][/h3]

Wayward Strand is a part of the Melbourne International Games Week (MIGW) showcase, which is starting now - [b]Sep 30th, 10am PDT / Oct 1st, 3am AEST[/b]. We'd love to invite you to check out our demo, which is available from the start of the event. Here's a handy widget thingie that you can use to go to our page to download it:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1080450/Wayward_Strand/

It's been quite a while since we updated our demo (our last one was built in October 2019!) so there's a lot of new features in there to have a look at. I've written more about the new demo features further down this post, but I'll tell you about MIGW first.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]

[h3]Melbourne International Games Week[/h3]

Affectionately known as MIGW (Mig-Wuh), Melbourne International Games Week is an annual celebration of all things Australian games. During MIGW there are loads of events and parties, sales, conferences and so on. Developers use it as an opportunity to catch up or get together at the pub, and it's also the time when all sorts of industry folks from Asia, Africa, Europe, The Americas and Oceania travel 'down under' to meet or give talks, and to do business (sometimes also at the pub!)

Specifically, MIGW highlights games made in Victoria, which is one of Australia's largest states, and definitely the most prolific for game developers - mostly because there's some funding support available for developers here. Lots of game developers from around Australia and even New Zealand move to Melbourne to chase their development dreams, and Wayward Strand wouldn't be able to be made without support from both Film Victoria and Creative Victoria. These are state-government bodies here, and both do a lot to bolster the entire industry from the ground up.

Some of the events which happen during MIGW include PAX Australia, and the amazing Parallels Showcase, which is part of the [url=https://www.freeplay.net.au/]Freeplay Independent Games Festival.[/url]

The Freeplay Parallels Showcase is our favourite games event each year. It puts a spotlight on some incredible local games, and always fills us with inspiration and hope for videogames. I'm sure this year will be no different - and even better, it's free! You can [url=http://trybooking.com/BTUYG]register for a ticket here,[/url] and I've embedded this year's trailer too, to whet your appetite!

[previewyoutube=uMyrR5NqXW0;full][/previewyoutube]

We want to thank Creative Victoria for putting together this special Steam Event as part of MIGW 2021. It will be highlighting several Victorian-made games, including ours - there are so many fantastic developers here and I really hope you can find time to dig through the demos, through the sale and through all of the great streams and talks happening.

[h3]Streaming[/h3] 
We'll be doing a live stream - a playthrough of our new demo and it's features, as well as looping some of our other streams from other events, such as LudoNarraCon, so be sure to check them out.

If you'd like to catch our live stream...[i]live[/i], it'll be happening on the MIGW event page as well as on our steam page at:

[i]11AM AEST October 1st
5PM PDT September 30th[/i]

(You can just subscribe to the event linked to this post, and you'll get notified when the stream is about to go live!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6131678ae69ca45b634709144ab57d3daebece49.png[/img]


There are seriously so many great games and developers to check out during the event. It’s impossible to cherry-pick our favourites without just showing our mates off - so please explore it yourself.
I really think your type of game will be there, whatever it is, because there’s [b]so[/b] much good and diverse work being made here in Victoria!

Now, about that new demo...


[h2]The Demo:[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/65b7b0159f41bf911e72cdab72e1019e4fc76f2d.gif[/img]

New demo! New demo!!!

We decided to make a new demo for this event. We've actually been working really hard on some other things, mostly on what we're calling a 'Day One Playable', which will serve as a production guide for us as we head towards release. Knowing how long it takes us to make 'Day One Playable' will hopefully tell us how long it'll take us to make Day Two and Day Three playable too. Then we will have 3 days playable, which is a finished Wayward Strand.

[b]SIKE!!!!![/b]

Nah, there's always more to do. We're working on the beginning of the game too, and the ending (both have been really exciting work, it's fun to develop bits of the game outside of the time spent on the ship). We're also busy working on some exciting VO stuff which I am sure we will blog about when that process starts, and as always we are working with our accessibility and cultural consultants to make sure Wayward Strand can be enjoyed by as close to everyone as possible.

The new demo has a few tastes of what we've done for Day One Playable so far, including some [i]lovely[/i] new UI improvements, a bunch of new scenes (and even new characters). Various visual improvements here and there, although most of that will plop together like baking a cake which we'll share once it's finished baking. Trust me, it's yummy, (and yes I licked the bowl.)

Does the new demo have bugs? Probably! Hopefully not too many. With a game like ours which has [i]so many[/i] moving parts I can't help but wonder, as I write this (about a week before we finish it), if we'll find some weird stuff in there.

As I mentioned, we’re going to be [b]doing a live stream[/b] during the MIGW event, where we’ll be playing the new demo and [b]exploring some of the new features[/b] - so come along to see those from our perspective, or watch the replay as it loops throughout the event.

[h3]That’s all folks![/h3]

Thanks so much for following along as we make this beautiful game.

I hope you enjoy the new demo, and I also hope you enjoy the MIGW Event on Steam.
Thanks again to Creative Victoria for the initiative.

Goldie, and [i]ghost pattern[/i].

notes.title: Directing Virtual Characters in Wayward Strand, Part 1
notes.content:
After [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1080450/view/3043850633882336474]my last post[/url], on how we’ve integrated ink and Timeline, there was some interest in how we use Unity’s Timeline tool to do things like trigger animations on characters.

Over the course of making Wayward Strand, we've developed a solution for this that we're pretty happy with. Put simply, we use Timeline to set parameters on our characters' Animator Controllers  - but we've developed quite a bit of scaffolding around this, as well as a useful categorisation structure for our animations.

There's quite a bit that goes into all this, so I'll cover it over a couple of posts  -  this first one will focus on the Animator Controllers, and I'll start by going into the reasoning behind why we went for this approach.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/1_Casey_Looks_At_Photograph.gif[/img]

Our problem space for animations in Wayward Strand is borne out of our game’s unique, simultaneous story structure. We wanted Wayward Strand to feel like an interactive theatre experience like Sleep No More, where the continuous location and physicality of the actors is such an important part of what makes that experience unique.

You see the character in their highlighted, plot-critical moment, where they perform the key action, or have that impactful interaction, that their story is structured around - but you also see the character [b]after [/b]this moment, when they have to move, in character, from one location to another. You also see them in their quiet moments, where they spend time in a room or space feeling satisfied, confused, expectant, or disconsolate - sometimes for considerable stretches of time.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/2_SleepNoMore_Reflection.jpg[/img]

In a real-time, criss-crossing story structure, these wobbly, windy arcs of heightened action and quietude/reflection are a joy to experience, and part of that joy comes from the [b]choice [/b]you make in who to follow - who to spend time with at any point in the story.

In a linear storytelling format, like a film, whenever you have a quiet moment, it’s because the director decided that you’ll have a quiet moment at that specific point in the story. Your moment-to-moment experience has been foreseen; planned; designed. But in a simultaneous storytelling format, you’re choosing to have that quiet moment, or happening upon it, while still existing inside the story’s world.

In attempting to capture this feeling in a videogame, we knew that we wanted our characters to live as continuously as we could manage within the world. This means that they’re generally not snapping from one state to another - the camera isn’t cutting away from them and then cutting back, allowing you to snap their animation state, or even load in an entirely new version of the character to handle a particular story moment.

Our characters exist in the world - performing a variety of actions, participating in scenes, having their quiet moments - and they do so continuously throughout each day, regardless of whether the player is near them or not.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/3_Lily_Interrogates_Neil.gif[/img]

The solution we landed on for Wayward Strand was a structure where we split most animations into belonging to one of two categories - [b]BodyPose [/b]and [b]Activity[/b]. Using this logical structure, we realised that we’d be able to run a lot of complex character movement through systems, without having to worry exactly about how the movement is managed on the code-side. This categorisation also helped significantly in determining which animations to develop, and what their requirements were.

I want to give a shoutout to Kalonica in particular here, who really came up with this logical solution as we were discussing our requirements and desires for the game, and convinced me of certain elements which I had thought would be limiting, but haven’t been in practice, and have actually turned out to be a really important part of having a feasible system come together that actually works.

The BodyPose/Activity solution required a very specific structure inside Unity’s animator controllers, and a setup where there is one Parameter directly linked to each BodyPose/Activity, named exactly the same as that BodyPose/Activity. There’s a bit to go over, so I’ll describe the way we set up the AnimatorControllers, then we’ll go through the parameters and how we trigger transitions between different states, and finally we’ll see the whole system in action. We’ll be looking at the animations of Ida, one of our characters, and by the end, we’ll be breaking down this set of transitions, where Ida goes from standing, to holding her knitting up to inspect it.


[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/4_Ida_Sits_And_Knits.gif[/img]

A BodyPose is generally a fixed state in which a character [i]could [/i]do a lot of different things - Standing, Sitting, Lying in Bed, etc. These BodyPoses live at the top level of the hierarchy, and each is represented by a StateMachine.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/5_Ida_BaseStateMachine.png[/img]

A general rule that we follow for BodyPoses is that they go through their default BodyPose when transitioning from one to the other (the default is Standing for ambulant characters). I think we’d be able to break this rule if we needed to, but so far, it’s made sense - because if a character is transitioning from one BodyPose to another, generally they’re moving from interacting with one prop, to interacting with a different one.

Let’s have a look inside the [i]Body_SittingLowChair [/i]StateMachine.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/6_Ida_BodyPose_SittingLowChair.png[/img]

Each BodyPose (except for Standing) is generally structured in this way - there’s an [i]In [/i]State/Animation, a [i]Doing [/i]State/Animation, and an [i]Out [/i]State/Animation. The [i]In [/i]plays its animation almost to the end, then transitions to [i]Doing[/i], and [i]Doing [/i]plays a looping animation, and will transition to [i]Out [/i]when the [i]Body_SittingLowChair [/i]parameter is no longer set.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/7_Ida_In_Doing_Out.gif[/img]

From the [i]In [/i]and [i]Doing [/i]states, there are transitions also set up that go to each of the Activities that are in the BodyPose - and from the Activities there are transitions back to [i]Doing[/i], or directly to [i]Out[/i], to allow for smoother transitions when going from a BodyPose+Activity to an entirely different BodyPose.

I can see most people looking at this (especially if you’ve worked with Unity’s AnimatorControllers before), and those overlapping transition arrows, and thinking “oh god, that looks like a nightmare”. And.. it kinda is! Which is why, after we had defined this structure and decided to invest in it for the majority of animations across all characters, we developed some EditorScript tools to help us automate the process.

In the following gif, I’m using one of the buttons we’ve added through EditorScripts to set up the default transitions for the Activity - the transitions to and from, including those additional ones from [i]In [/i]and to [i]Out[/i]. (The script also adds any relevant parameters to transitions where necessary.)

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/8_Ida_Add_Activity.gif[/img]

Even though it takes some time to figure out and implement Unity’s editor scripting, automating these kinds of processes is really handy, because it ultimately saves time, reduces the chance for errors that you have to track down, and gives you some good defaults to work with - each of those states/transitions can still be modified after the script has gone through and done that initial set up, but you’ve got a baseline that will work in game.

Okay, let’s go one layer deeper, into the Activities themselves. One of our most complicated examples is Ida’s animations for doing her knitting.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/9_Ida_Activity_HoldingKnitting.png[/img]

You can see that we start out with a similar structure to the BodyPoses - [i]In -> Doing -> Out[/i] - but that instead of a deeper level of specificity in here, we have a bunch of States/StateMachines that are linked to generic parameters - [i]Pause[/i], [i]SpecialLoop[/i], [i]SpecialOnce[/i], etc.

For the additional States at this level beyond [i]Doing[/i], we’ve landed on the term [b]ActivityModifier [/b]- these animations “modify” the Activity, but the character is still fundamentally, logically within the Activity (and the associated BodyPose, one level up). ActivityModifier is a bit of a fiddly name, but works for our purposes. We start out all of our Activities with this basic structure, which allows us to add specific animations that are driven by generic parameters.

For Ida’s knitting animations, she can start knitting ([i]In[/i]), loop knitting ([i]Doing[/i]), and stop knitting ([i]Out[/i]). She can also rest from her knitting loop without exiting the Activity ([i]Pause[/i]). This Activity also has 3 special states - Ida lifts the knitting up to inspect it ([i]SpecialLoop[/i]), Ida puts the knitting down into her lap ([i]SpecialLoop2[/i]), and a [i]SpecialOnce [/i]State that isn’t currently used, but could be used for a ‘once-off’ animation, like one where Ida sighs while knitting, or realises she’s made a mistake and back-tracks in her knitting a bit.

The reason these states are named in this generic way, and use generic parameters, is so that we can trigger the parameter regardless of what BodyPose/Activity the character is in. For example, the modifier we use most often is the [i]Pause [/i]modifier - it’s great to have these Activities set up such that a character can doing an Activity (like knitting, or reading, or eating), and then pause the doing of that activity so that they can eg. respond to someone, or can just pause to take a moment within a scene.

In Wayward Strand, there are scenes that are triggered by the player’s presence (by Casey asking a character a question, or a character talking with Casey because she’s in the room), where we don’t know exactly when the scene might play out. But, by using generic parameters like [i]Pause[/i], we can still direct Ida within the scene, during a conversation, to [i]Pause [/i]or resume [i]Doing[/i], regardless of whether at that time she happens to be knitting, or drinking tea, or doing something else.

This means we can create nuanced portrayals of characters, even when we don’t know what they’re currently doing, through using these generic ActivityModifiers, along with other elements of character direction, like specifying which way their head is facing (whether Ida is looking at Casey or whether she’s looking at whatever she’s doing), and other animations which might only affect characters’ heads, like talking, sighing or nodding.

[img]https://waywardstrand.com/blog/directing_virtual_characters_p1/1_Casey_Looks_At_Photograph.gif[/img]

Returning to the gif from the start of the post, we can see this in practice. When Casey asks Ida about the photograph in her room, she first pauses her knitting, then puts it down into her lap as she responds.

In the next post in this two-part series, we’ll explore the parameters that drive the transitions inside the Animator Controllers, as well as how all of this integrates with Unity’s Timeline tool.

notes.title: Using ink and Unity's Timeline to make Wayward Strand
notes.content:
Hi there - I’m Jason, a member of the team making Wayward Strand.

Now that we’re getting closer to finishing and releasing Wayward Strand, we thought we’d start sharing a bit more of our development process as it happens. As we’ve been developing Wayward Strand for a few years now, this post is a mix of what we’re focusing on right now, and catching you up to where our team is at with our tech and development process.

So, one of the challenges we had to overcome when deciding to make a fully-3D real-time narrative game with complex, animated characters as an indie team was: [b]how?[/b]

This is something that’s been a conundrum for indie developers of narrative games for a while now, with some opting to forgo visualising characters all-together. For instance Fullbright, the creators of Gone Home and Tacoma, are only just including fully visualised characters in their upcoming Open Roads, and in their previous games, they cleverly designed around the need to include fully visualised characters to tell their stories.

While our answer to this was partially just ‘let’s just do it and see how we go’, and we’ve run into plenty of trouble along the way, we have found what I think is a pretty good combination of existing / open-source tools, which has enabled us to create a game of the size and scope that we had been dreaming of.

The first of these is [i][url=https://www.inklestudios.com/ink/]ink[/url][/i] - Inkle’s scripting language, which they’ve very generously provided as an open-source tool for developers. [i]Ink[/i] fulfills a similar role to narrative tools such as Twine or Yarn Spinner - it allows you to construct complex interactive narratives in a way where you can easily plug it into a game engine. Astrologaster writer Katharine Neil has [url=https://medium.com/@haikus_by_KN/twine-2-vs-ink-a-quick-and-dirty-unity-integration-comparison-99fe1e4549d]a great write-up[/url] of how to integrate [i]ink[/i], as well as Twine and Yarn Spinner, with Unity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/fcf2c7352b6b418ff91c5622be8a5a4f876f0ce4.png[/img]
[i]One of our scene files, open in the Inky editor.[/i]

There are many reasons we love [i]ink[/i], but one in particular is the narrative momentum that it encourages through its design. Writing with [i]ink[/i] feels like less like designing a circuit board than writing a script for theatre or the screen - while it can handle any level of complexity you need, your initial focus is the blank page and the written word, and you can add interactive complexity as you go.

[i]Incidentally, Inkle have just released [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1546920/Overboard/]Overboard![/url] - a murder mystery game that uses ink as the backbone for its dynamic narrative - check it out! And if you use ink or think it’s a cool tool, definitely consider [url=https://www.patreon.com/inkle]supporting them on Patreon[/url].[/i]

We are using [i]ink[/i] in tandem with Unity’s Timeline tool.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/c2e5c47ca9161e3cee86367463c2d714988d5a01.png[/img]

[i]One of our lines in Unity’s Timeline tool.[/i]

Timelines are a feature of Unity that allow you to synchronise clips that they call “playables” to a time axis - it’s basically a programmable sequencer for events that can happen in your game, like animations playing, characters moving around, sounds triggering, etc. If you’d like to learn more about Timeline and how to use it, [url=https://www.blog.radiator.debacle.us/2019/11/practical-primer-to-using-unity.html]this post by Robert Yang[/url] is a great place to start.

So, how have we plugged these two different tools together for Wayward Strand?

Early on, we decided that the [i]ink[/i] [b]Line[/b] would be the key building block of the game. This would limit us in terms of [i]ink’s[/i] capability to dynamically build lines based on logic, but this is a limitation we would have to take on anyway to include voice-over, and also to make localisation easier - including support for each of these was a goal for the game from an early stage.

From there, we planned out our integration with Unity. We wanted the ability to ‘direct’ our interactive scenes - to be able to modify any part of it, including being able to quickly and easily direct the timing of any aspect of the scene.

We also needed a way to trigger animations, character look-at changes, camera movements, and other minor Unity details - and while we could have run all of that stuff from [i]ink[/i], we were keen to draw a line between the writing process and the ‘scene direction’ process, which would allow us to focus on each of these processes in turn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/914c46ae4f512e3406d329723ddb53eab6b316c7.png[/img]
[i]Our old line-editing tool, including a few features that we’ve cut to reduce scope.[/i]

Our initial integration actually happened before Timeline was released - we developed a data structure on the Unity side which stored data per [i]ink[/i] Line, in arrays of “components” (so, each line could have a Dialogue component, multiple Movement components, and so forth). This component data was automatically created for each line as [i]ink[/i] files were compiled, in a dictionary linked to the [i]ink[/i] file.

When Timeline was released, we quickly switched over, starting with a similar solution. We realised we could (with a bit of hackery, at the time), automatically generate Timeline assets, and we started by creating them for each [i]ink[/i] Line, as we were doing before. While this is a fairly brute-force solution, and working with the scenes in Unity line-by-line can sometimes be counter-intuitive, it has lasted us over the course of the project.


So, our current pipeline is as follows:

1. We’ve created a custom version of the [i]ink[/i] compiler, which creates a unique line identifier based off of the text in the line, the current knot/stitch, and a unique identifier for the [i]ink[/i] file that the line is in. It then prefixes this unique line identifier to the line itself. 

A fun little issue with generating the unique line identifier is that if any line is exactly the same as another in a particular scene or knot, it will be generated with the same id, so we have to add a “differentiator” on to the end of them - a little tag that denotes which of the two lines it is.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/f1c32e164077bc8e8786e243cfe0440900155411.png[/img]
[i]Another scene from the game.[/i]

Our modified compiler also generates a custom json file, alongside the [i]ink[/i] json file, which includes a list of all the [i]ink[/i] lines, so that we can easily process them on the Unity side. (You can see all our semi-hacky modifications to the [i]ink[/i] compiler [url=https://github.com/ghostpattern/ink/tree/LineMarkupPlugin]on Github[/url].)

2. In Unity, we parse the [i]ink[/i] Story to collect tag information about the scene, or knots inside the scene, and then we use the [i]ink[/i] Line list from the custom json file to generate a Timeline asset for each line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6f54bb35555cc3fdc0eb9985da0312935aceb463.png[/img]
[i]Generated Timeline assets for the scene in the Unity project view.[/i]

These Timeline assets get set up with a few default tracks and clips:
[list]
[*] a LineLength track/clip, which determines how long until the next line in the scene should be triggered (the length of time that a line lasts for is initially set to a value that’s calculated based on the amount of characters in the line);
[*] a Dialogue track/clip, which cues our VO when the clip is triggered, as well as handling our character mouth shapes and talking-animation-related behaviour (including head-turning);
[*] a Subtitle track/clip, which is used to trigger our speech bubbles, and also potential subtitles when that accessibility option is activated (these clips process the Line through a Dialogue system that handles the potential for translation).
[/list]

3. Finally, we have a scene direction tool that exists alongside the Timeline, which allows us to easily move between lines in the scene (backward, forward, or jumping to a particular line), as well as displaying a bunch of helpful buttons that quickly add additional clips to the timeline - animation state change clips, movement clips, character head look-at clips, and so forth.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/371b771f710e1f78b8a596c7f233fae9e045709b.png[/img]
[i]It all comes together in Unity - this is our project in Direction mode.[/i]

What this fundamentally means is that, when we go from our [i]ink[/i] script, across to Unity, the majority of the data is already set up for us. Characters may not move in the scene until a scene direction pass happens, but they’ll talk with each other, Casey’s options will pop up on screen when they’re meant to, and the scene can be played from start to finish.

It also means that, when doing the scene directing pass, most of the data already exists, ready to be tweaked. We can quickly drag the LineLength clips around to get some more interesting behaviour occurring (like characters speaking over the top of one another, or a weighty pause before a response), and the only data we need to ‘create’ (other than movement data) is generally the finer-detail scene direction.

There are some other fun details that I haven’t covered here - like how we respond to edits in our [i]ink[/i] scenes after they’ve been imported once, or how we link our Playable clips to particular characters without using Timeline’s ‘binding’ functionality - but, even though we clearly have put a lot of effort in to make this all work, it still feels like a significant amount of the heavy lifting is being done by Timeline and [i]ink[/i] - we certainly couldn’t have done all of this as well as building a scripting language and a scriptable sequencer.


This pipeline has been years in the making for our small team, and describing it has made me extra proud of all the work we’ve put in. Look forward to sharing more over the next few months!

notes.title: Live-stream: Accessibility in Indie Games
notes.content:
May 20th is the 10th annual [url=https://globalaccessibilityawarenessday.org]Global Accessibility Awareness Day[/url]! To celebrate, we're announcing that the wonderful Cameron Hopkinson (they/them) is providing accessibility consultation and advice for Wayward Strand, and that we will be hosting a live-stream where Cameron and Maize Wallin (they/them) discuss accessibility in Wayward Strand, and in indie games generally. The stream will begin at [b]May 20th 10:00 pm PT / May 21st 3:00 pm AEST[/b]

Having a focus on accessibility during game design and development is incredibly important - it reduces barriers to your experience for so many players. For the other game makers out there, here are a few links to some really useful resources:

[url=http://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com]http://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com[/url] - this is an list of accessibility feature and improvements for games, grouped by ease-of-implementation! It's an incredibly useful resource - thanks so much to all the accessibility experts that put it together.

[url=https://www.accessunlocked.games]https://www.accessunlocked.games[/url] - this is a collective that Cameron is a part of, whose goal is to put a spotlight on accessibility, both in games and in game development, helping disabled developers connect to each other.

https://twitter.com/ga_conf The Games Accessibility Conference is a regular event including talks and meetups around accessibility in games. Many talks from previous events are [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCKWG26bBd7TOiaLtc_crqvw/videos]accessible on their Youtube channel[/url]; it's a treasure trove of information.

Look forward to more info from us on accessibility in Wayward Strand, and if you have accessibility needs and played the demo, or are keen to play Wayward Strand, reach out and let us know what accessibility options/considerations would have the most impact for you!

notes.title: Development Continues!
notes.content:
Hi, again! We haven't spoken too much about development recently, so we just wanted to answer some questions about what's been happening, and where we’re at on the road to getting Wayward Strand into your Steam library.

[h2]When will Wayward Strand be released?[/h2]

Our current plan is to release in the second half of 2021 - while there are some elements of that plan to fall into place, we feel that we’re in a good spot to finish out Wayward Strand and actually get it into your hands!

[h2]What’s been happening lately?[/h2]

For most of this year we’ve been working on Wayward Strand part-time, or in between other work - progress has been slower than we had previously projected, but things have still been moving forward. In particular, the dialogue has come a long way since the start of the year, primarily thanks to our writer Georgia Symons.

Many of our scenes were initially planned out back in 2016, and seeing these scenes in particular get to the point where their dialogue is written and staging is laid out has been really special.

We’ve also spent a lot of this year showing Wayward Strand at virtual events and getting people to play our demo, which includes a section of the first day. We showcased at LudoNarracon 2020, the Steam Summer Festival and Yogscast’s Tiny Teams Festival, and were also featured in the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AwCNzOPR8Ck]Wholesome Direct Showcase[/url]. Getting into live-streaming Wayward Strand and sharing our development process was a big change for us, but we’ve enjoyed it, and it’s been wonderful to discover how many people are interested in this strange and beautiful experience.

If you missed these events while they were happening, you can catch up on recordings of our live-streams for LudoNarraCon on our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AwCNzOPR8Ck]Youtube page[/url] (there’s literally hours of us talking Wayward on there!) And if you’re keen to chat with us and the rest of the community, come join the [url=https://discord.gg/KDAMU3N]Wayward Strand Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/5737026fc2a4d30161f8d6c60e1201a0409e80c2.jpg[/img]

Finally, I wanted to mention that there have been some exciting (and rather time-consuming) elements of our plan to complete and release Wayward Strand that have come together over the past few months - there’s not much we can mention specifically here, except to say that we’ll have some exciting news as we get closer to launch about [i]where[/i] Wayward Strand will be popping up.

[hr][/hr]

But for now, we’ll just keep tinkering away on this thing, and we’ll let you know every now and then how it’s going. This project has been a longer-than-expected labour of love, and it can sometimes be surprising to think that we are all still excited about continuing to work on it, five years in. But we are, and we really look forward to the day when you can play Wayward Strand for yourself, and see all that we’ve put into it.

We hope you stay safe, and stay well, and that you get to spend some time (virtually, if necessary) with friends and loved ones throughout the holidays.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/270b0517767e013416d3ed49fd2ee8655213c229.png[/img]

If you've never heard of Wayward Strand before: well, it's very lovely to meet you! Wayward Strand is our heartfelt interactive story set on board an airborne hospital. You play as Casey, a slightly rebellious fourteen year old, and explore the ship, getting to know the characters on board, and exploring their lives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/2258282fdb585033c9d0619c3894ed0290270b3d.jpg[/img]

A special feature of our game is that the entire ship and its motley crew of characters all live out their lives as you play. They don't wait around for you to visit them before their story moves forward - each character has their own story, and it plays out as time passes aboard the ship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/5d8c470b071f800966ea35bd27f6df261c85dde4.png[/img]

This makes Wayward Strand feel really different, as a game, and an experience - it's almost like a living world. As you explore the ship, you'll come across characters who are doing their own things - following their own paths, having their own interactions - and each time you play through the three days that Casey visits the ship, you'll only see a fraction of the entire story of Wayward Strand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/e440d302560c187f8d49053e00741d505810743f.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Welcome to the Wayward Strand booth!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/6177765ca130407c8cc9fd017d9ff4bd9ea74891.png[/img]

Hi, and thanks for coming to check out Wayward Strand at the Steam Summer Festival!

Wayward Strand is our experimental and heartfelt story game, in which you play as Casey, a teenager who explores an airborne hospital and gets to know the patients and staff inside. Our latest demo is available to try, we'd love you to check it out, and then let us know what you think of it - you can do this on our [url=https://discord.gg/MszHdW9]Discord[/url] or our [url=https://twitter.com/WaywardStrand]Twitter[/url]. You can also connect with us during the livestreams we're doing throughout the festival!

As you play the demo, you'll notice an interesting mechanic - all the characters aboard the ship have their own stories, and they each live out their day, independent of what you (as Casey) are doing. You can choose to follow a particular character to see what goes on with them, to spend time with them and chat, or just to wander around to see what you happen upon at a particular time in a particular place.

Our demo is of the beginning section of the game, and doesn't take too long to play - about 15 minutes - but you can play it multiple times if you'd like, to see all the different things that are going on during the first morning on the ship.

[h2]About Us[/h2]

Our team is based in Melbourne, Australia, and we've been working on Wayward Strand for a few years now. We all came together around this unique idea, having been inspired by interactive theatre like Sleep No More, and during development we've been figuring out our development processes as we make the game.

We work in a pretty unique way for an indie team - for instance, Wayward Strand is set on the coast in Victoria, on Bunurong land, and we have done several fun research trips there, spending time in the area as a team, wandering around and discussing the experience, the history and the characters.

We also do a lot of consultation, because while the airship and the characters are fictional, it's set in a historical context (1978 Australia), and we want to draw as much as we can from the real history of the time, as well as including stories informed by our discussions with members of the Bunurong community, who are the Indigenous people of the land where Wayward Strand is set.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/5dc5d1a13203ff75b56addf81df57e055f519692.png[/img]

That's (some of) the team up there! From left to right, it's Russell (programming), Maize (sound & music), Jason (production, writing, & programming), Kalonica (art & animation), Goldie (art direction) - and Aspen (tech art) on the far right has been lovingly photoshopped in by Goldie.

Here we are on one of our research trips, when we went down to Inverloch for a few days to explore, capture audio, and discuss the history of the area with the local historical society:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35872257/d7b0ed19d59498b16502dae023558cc9912b2400.jpg[/img]

There are a bunch more wonderful team members, collaborators and consultants that have contributed to Wayward Strand over the course of development as well - we're really a little community of our own now.

That’s all for the moment - thanks for stopping by! We really hope you enjoy the demo, and if you do, please [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1080450/Wayward_Strand/]add us to your Wishlist[/url] - that way you can be notified when the game is released and you can play it in full.

Lots of love,
The Wayward Strand team
